text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The National Bank of Slovakia said the reason for not paying its profit into the state budget in the first half of this year was its prorgamme of "monetary sterilisation". The NBS said it would fulfil its obligations to the budget in the second half of the year.
- The National Property Fund (NPF), the state privatisation agency, rejected fears that it would not be able to reimburse citizens for their privatisation bonds in 2001 due to liquidity problems.
- The NPF said its share portfolio now totalled 90 billion crowns.
- Britain's Tesco Plc is to start complete reconstruction of the supermarket network in Slovakia bought this spring from the U.S. K-Mart.
- Singapore Airlines is to open a representative office in Bratislava. The airline, however, does not intend to inaugurate direct routes to and from Bratislava.

PRAVDA - Jan Gabriel, president of the largest Slovak bank VUB, said Slovak banks were undercapitalised and that the largest financial institutions, such as VUB, would need at least to double their capital, for example through subordinated debt. Gabriel said VUB was negotiating unspecified offers from foreign banks, but the bank would have first to stabilise the situation of its risky assets.
- Gabriel said the Slovak banking sector was not threatened by a crisis similar to that in the Czech Republic.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Steel maker VSZ is attempting to acquire control over the investment fund Regionfond through its 20 percent stake in the largest insurer Slovenska Poistovna, which holds 13 percent in the fund. Poistovna already initiated changes to the fund statutes and management, but previous fund officials claimed the moves were illegal and took the case to court.
- According to government plans Slovakia should have a balanced state budget in the year 2000.

- Export-import company Martimex, which exports about 20 percent of Slovak engineering production, expects its turnover to total seven billion crowns this year. Martimex's main commercial partners are Germany, India and the states of former Soviet Union. The firm said it planned to expand its activities to China and U.S.
